title: Applied ML Evals: Integrated Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Onboarding & Regression Playbook
author: Priya Nandakumar
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood's integrated approach to applied ML evaluations: the eval harness, prompt sets and benchmarks, model onboarding steps, quality guardrails, quantization profile guidance, and a regression triage playbook. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML owners, and SREs who operate inference services. The goal is to ensure consistent, repeatable quality checks and automated regressions detection during model onboarding, optimization, and rollouts.

Scope

- Eval harness: CI-integrated evaluation framework used for model validation, pre-release gating, and periodic drift checks.
- Prompt sets & benchmarks: curated input families and scoring criteria for functional and safety checks.
- Model onboarding: standardized checklist and automated tests for adding models to the serving catalog.
- Quality guardrails: automated thresholds and human review triggers for quality regressions.
- Quantization profiles: recommended quantization configurations and performance/quality tradeoff documentation.
- Regression triage: runbook for incident response when a regression is detected.

High-level Architecture

1) Eval Harness
- Implementation: pytest-based harness with modular evaluation steps, containerized runners, and results output in both JSON (structured) and HTML reports for review.
- Data sources: synthetic prompt sets, customer-derived holdouts (anonymized), and open benchmarks.
- Integration points: CI (GitHub Actions), model registry (model metadata tags), monitoring (Prometheus metrics export for eval pass/fail), and alerting (PagerDuty / Slack channel).

2) Prompt Sets and Benchmarks
- Catalog: prompt sets are organized by intent and difficulty (smoke, core, stress). Each set contains: prompt id, example inputs, expected output types, gold labels where applicable, and evaluation scripts.
- Scoring: per-example scoring functions (exact match, BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) plus task-level aggregations (median, 75th percentile).
- Maintenance cadence: quarterly reviews for drift and coverage; add new edge-case sets after major product features.

3) Model Onboarding Guide (Summary)
- Ownership: model owner must be declared in model metadata (owner_email).
- Required artifacts:
  - model-card.md (description, training data provenance, licencing)
  - baseline eval report (eval_harness JSON output)
  - latencies & resource profile (p50/p95 token latency, GPU memory, KV cache behavior)
  - quantization compatibility report (if quantized)
- Automated checks (run on PR):
  1. Lint model-card and metadata schema.
  2. Run full eval harness (smoke + core prompt sets).
  3. Run perf microbench (seq_len=128/512) and memory checks.
  4. Produce canary config for staged rollout.

Onboarding Checklist (numbered)
1. Create model entry in model registry with owner, tags, and semantic version.
2. Attach model-card.md and baseline eval JSON.
3. Add prompt-set coverage note (what tasks this model is expected to support).
4. CI: ensure PR passes eval harness; if not, document deviations and file a triage ticket.
5. Request canary rollout to dev cluster for production-like runs.
6. After canary, run A/B evals and monitor quality metrics for 48-72 hours.
7. Approve for general serving or revert and iterate.

Quality Guardrails and Thresholds

- Core SLOs (applied-eval):
  - Task accuracy (core classification tasks): must be >= baseline_model_accuracy - 1.5 percentage points.
  - Top-1 correctness (generation): median correctness score >= baseline_median - 0.05 (absolute).
  - Safety checks: zero tolerance for high-severity safety violations; any flagged high-severity triggers immediate rollback.
  - Latency: p95 per-token latency must not exceed baseline_p95 * 1.25 for same HW class.

- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - Eval suite fail rate >= 10% across core prompt sets -> page oncall ML engineering.
  - Metric regression (task-level) drops > 5% absolute -> create regression ticket and begin triage.
  - Quantized model quality drop > 3% absolute compared to FP16 baseline -> require manual review and acceptance by model owner.

Quantization Profiles Guidance

- Profiles are versioned artifacts describing node-level quantization config (e.g., 8-bit GPTQ, 4-bit data types, per-channel vs per-tensor). Each profile must include: profile_id, target hardware class, expected memory saving, expected quality delta (estimated), and verification eval pack.
- Recommended default profiles:
  - q8_per_channel_v1: balanced latency and quality for RTX-class GPUs. Expected quality delta <= 1.5% on core tasks.
  - q4_dynamic_v1: aggressive memory saving for constrained hosts; expected quality delta 2.5-4% and recommended only for non-critical workloads.
- Verification: for any profile applied to a model, run the quantization verification pack (subset of core prompt sets + stress cases). Quantized model must meet the profile's declared quality delta bounds or be flagged for manual review.

Regression Triage Playbook (runbook steps)

1) Detection and Triage
- Trigger sources: automated eval harness runs (CI or scheduled), production monitors (drift detectors, A/B test comparisons), customer incident reports.
- Initial step: create a regression incident in the triage board with tags (model_id, eval_suite, metric_delta, detection_time).

2) Quick Triage (15-60 mins)
- Re-run failing evals against:
  - the new candidate model binary,
  - the previous production model binary,
  - an earlier baseline snapshot if available.
- Collect logs: eval JSON outputs, seed/settings, hardware class, quantization profile, tokenizer version.
- Determine whether regression is systemic (across tasks/prompt sets) or localized (one prompt family).

3) Escalation and Remediation
- If systemic drop in core tasks (>5% absolute): page ML oncall, block rollout, mark model as not-ready.
- If localized: create a focused investigation ticket assigned to model owner and Applied ML.
- For quantization-specific regressions: revert to FP16 for affected traffic or apply a safer quantization profile (e.g., q8_per_channel_v1).

4) Root Cause Analysis (RCA)
- Typical RCA dimensions:
  - Prompt set coverage gaps or changed prompts (prompt drift).
  - Tokenizer upgrades or normalization changes.
  - Hidden data leakage changing evaluation expectations.
  - New sampling/decoding defaults (temperature/top-p) introduced in runtime.
  - Quantization-induced distribution shift in logits.
- RCA deliverables: chronology, repro script, minimal failing prompt set, corrective action plan, owner, and ETA.

5) Postmortem and Preventive Actions
- Runbook requires a written postmortem within 72 hours for any regression that impacted serving traffic > 1% of production requests or exceeded 24 hours of degraded quality.
- Preventive actions may include expanding prompt sets, adding synthetic adversarial tests, pinning tokenizer/runtime versions, and improving canary durations.

Monitoring and Dashboards

- Required dashboards:
  - Eval pass/fail trend (daily/weekly) by model and prompt-family.
  - A/B quality delta dashboard with confidence intervals and traffic segmentation.
  - Quantization verification results and memory/latency tradeoff curves.
- Prometheus metrics (examples exported by harness):
  - applied_eval_suite_total{model_id, suite} - total examples executed
  - applied_eval_suite_failures{model_id, suite} - examples failing threshold
  - applied_eval_metric_delta{model_id, metric} - signed delta vs baseline

Example CI Snippet (YAML)

- The eval job is expected to run in CI with a reproducible container image and cache model artifacts via the artifact store. Example (conceptual):

  name: eval-harness
  on: [push, pull_request]
  jobs:
    run-eval:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Run eval harness
          run: |
            docker run --rm 
              -e MODEL_ID=${{ matrix.model }} 
              -v ${{ github.workspace }}:/workspace 
              redwood/eval-harness:stable 
              /workspace/eval_scripts/run_full_eval.sh --suite core --output /workspace/reports/${{ matrix.model }}.json

Operational Notes and Ownership

- Ownership matrix (examples):
  - Eval harness infra: infra-ml (oncall: infra-ml@redwood.internal)
  - Prompt set curation: Applied ML team (owners rotate quarterly)
  - Model onboarding gatekeeper: Model Platform (approvers: model-platform@redwood.internal)
  - Incident triage: ML oncall (pager duty) + SRE for perf incidents

- Review cadence: quarterly review of prompt sets, monthly scheduled evals for high-traffic models, and automatic scheduled evals (nightly) for models flagged as high-risk (by traffic or sensitivity).

Appendix: Common Troubleshooting Patterns

- Symptom: localized correctness drop on a single intent family.
  - Quick check: verify prompt set was not updated and tokenizer/version matches baseline.
  - If tokenizer changed, re-run tokenization diff and map gold labels accordingly.

- Symptom: quantized model degrades on rare prefixes.
  - Quick check: run quantization-verification pack and compare logits distribution to FP16 baseline.
  - If divergence observed, revert quantization profile and add failing prefixes to stress set.

- Symptom: CI eval flaps between runs.
  - Quick check: ensure deterministic seeds and identical runtime flags; check GPU preemption or memory pressure.
